question: The great poet and humanist writer Rabindra Nath Tagore returned his knighthood in protest of which incident?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore, a renowned poet and writer, renounced his **Knighthood** in protest against the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.
 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** took place on **April 13, 1919**, in **Amritsar, Punjab**.
 
• During the massacre, British troops under the command of **General Dyer** opened fire on a peaceful gathering, resulting in the death of hundreds of unarmed civilians.
 
• This brutal act deeply affected Tagore, prompting him to return his **Knighthood** as a form of protest.
 
• The incident is considered one of the darkest chapters in the history of British rule in India and played a significant role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Tagore's renunciation of the Knighthood was a symbolic gesture to express his outrage and solidarity with the victims of British colonial oppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bengal partition, 1905**

 
 
• It was officially announced on 19 July 1905 by Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• A new province of East Bengal and Assam was announced, with a population of 3.1 crores, and a Muslim-Hindu ratio of 3:2. Bengal, the western province, was overwhelmingly Hindu. 
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784**
 
 
• **​​**The Pitt’s India Act, of 1784 also called the** East India Company Act, 1784**.
 
• Pitt’s India Act, of 1784 was passed to rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773.
 
• It allowed the Court of Directors to manage commercial affairs but created a new body called the Board of Control to manage political affairs.
 
 
 
• **Kamagatamaru case, 1914**
 
 
• **​Komagatamaru **was a **Japanese ship **on which a group of Indians attempted to **immigrate to Canada in April 1914**.
 
• It carried **376 passengers from Punjab **and out of all** only 24 were admitted to Canada** and the rest were returned to India.
 
• The ship returned to Kolkata Port in September 1914, the passengers were asked to take the Punjab-bound train, which they refused and in conflict 22 people died.
